pinyin: bǎi wú yī yòng shì shū shēng
literal: a hundred · none · one · use · is · scholar
natural: of a hundred things, a scholar is good at none

meaning.en: A bitter, self-mocking remark that a bookish scholar is useful for nothing practical.
meaning.zh: 读书人手无缚鸡之力，百无一用；多为自嘲或感慨之语。

equivalents: a bookworm is good for nothing
the scholar is useless in practical affairs

examples.zh: 找工作屡屡碰壁，他自嘲百无一用是书生。
examples.en: Rejected again and again in his job search, he mocked himself: a scholar is good for nothing.

examples.zh: 修不好水管，她笑说百无一用是书生。
examples.en: Unable to fix the pipe, she joked that a bookworm is good for nothing.

examples.zh: 百无一用是书生，这句诗道出了多少读书人的无奈。
examples.en: 'A scholar is good for nothing' voices the helplessness of many an intellectual.

story.en: Huang Jingren, a poor Qing scholar, wrote: 'Nine in ten deserve a cold stare; a scholar is good for nothing at all' (十有九人堪白眼，百无一用是书生).
story.zh: 清代黄景仁《杂感》：“十有九人堪白眼，百无一用是书生。”

usage.en: Often self-deprecating; the first half of the couplet is 十有九人堪白眼.
usage.zh: 多作自嘲；上句为“十有九人堪白眼”。

pinyin: yán yǒu jìn ér yì wú qióng
literal: words · have · end · yet · meaning · no · limit
natural: the words end but the meaning goes on

meaning.en: The words come to an end but the meaning lingers on, said of rich, suggestive writing.
meaning.zh: 话语虽已说完，意味却悠长无尽，形容含蓄而耐人寻味。

examples.zh: 好诗往往言有尽而意无穷，读完让人回味很久。
examples.en: A good poem often leaves its meaning lingering after the words end, so one keeps savouring it.

examples.zh: 这部电影结尾含蓄，言有尽而意无穷。
examples.en: The film's ending is understated, the words stop but the meaning goes on.

examples.zh: 他的文章言有尽而意无穷。
examples.en: His essays end, but their meaning lingers.

story.en: Yan Yu, comparing the best poetry to echoes in the air and the moon in water, concludes that its words end but its meaning has no end.
story.zh: 南宋严羽《沧浪诗话·诗辨》论盛唐诗的妙处，如“空中之音，相中之色，水中之月，镜中之象，言有尽而意无穷”。

usage.en: Literary criticism; used to praise subtlety and implied meaning.
usage.zh: 文学评论用语，称赞含蓄、余味悠长。

pinyin: tài shān bù ràng tǔ rǎng
literal: Mount Tai · not · decline · soil
natural: Mount Tai does not refuse a clod of earth

meaning.en: Greatness comes from accepting everything, even the smallest contributions.
meaning.zh: 泰山不拒绝细小的土壤，所以才能高大；比喻包容各方才能成就大事。

examples.zh: 泰山不让土壤，团队要有容人之量。
examples.en: Mount Tai refuses no soil; a team needs generosity toward others.

examples.zh: 学校提倡泰山不让土壤，欢迎不同背景的学生。
examples.en: The school promotes 'Mount Tai refuses no soil' and welcomes students from all backgrounds.

examples.zh: 泰山不让土壤，一点一滴的积累成就大业。
examples.en: Mount Tai spurns no earth; little by little, great works are built.

story.en: Li Si, urging the king of Qin not to expel foreign officials, argued: 'Mount Tai does not decline a clod of earth, so it grew so great'.
story.zh: 李斯《谏逐客书》：“泰山不让土壤，故能成其大；河海不择细流，故能就其深。”

usage.en: Usually paired with 河海不择细流; formal, in speeches on tolerance.
usage.zh: 常与“河海不择细流”连用，较正式，多用于谈包容。

pinyin: wéi jīng wéi yī
literal: only · refined · only · single-minded
natural: be refined and be single-minded

meaning.en: Be thoroughly refined and wholly focused; a precept on pursuing the Way with undivided attention.
meaning.zh: 精心专一，一心一意；治学修身都要专注而精细。

examples.zh: 做学问要惟精惟一，不能心猿意马。
examples.en: In scholarship one must be refined and single-minded, with no wandering of the mind.

examples.zh: 工匠们惟精惟一，把一件事做到极致。
examples.en: The craftsmen are refined and single-minded, taking one thing to perfection.

examples.zh: 校训用“惟精惟一”勉励学生专心求学。
examples.en: The school motto, 'wéi jīng wéi yī', urges students to study with focus.

story.en: In the 'Counsels of the Great Yu', Shun tells Yu: 'The human mind is perilous, the mind of the Way is subtle; be refined, be single-minded, hold firmly to the middle' (the chapter is a later 'old-text' forgery, but the line has long been quoted).
story.zh: 《尚书·大禹谟》舜告诫禹：“人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允执厥中。”（今本《大禹谟》为晚出古文。）

date.zh: 东晋 · 4世纪（晚出古文《尚书》）

usage.en: Literary; mottoes and exhortations. The full line is 人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允执厥中.
usage.zh: 书面语，常作校训、勉语；全句为“人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允执厥中”。

pinyin: mín bù wèi sǐ
literal: people · not · fear · death
natural: when the people no longer fear death

meaning.en: When people no longer fear death, threats of execution cannot control them; a warning against harsh rule.
meaning.zh: 当百姓不再怕死时，以死刑威吓也无济于事；用来警示苛政。

equivalents: threats can't scare a desperate people
when the people no longer fear death

examples.zh: 民不畏死，奈何以死惧之，苛政终会引来反抗。
examples.en: 'If the people do not fear death, why frighten them with it?'; harsh rule invites rebellion in the end.

examples.zh: 史书上说民不畏死，是因为他们已走投无路。
examples.en: Histories say the people no longer feared death because they were out of options.

examples.zh: 民不畏死的背后，往往是长期的压迫。
examples.en: Behind 'the people no longer fear death' there is often long oppression.

story.en: Laozi ch. 74: 'If the people do not fear death, why frighten them with death?' (民不畏死，奈何以死惧之).
story.zh: 《老子》第七十四章：“民不畏死，奈何以死惧之？”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前5—前4世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 5th–4th c. BC

usage.en: Quoted in political and historical commentary; usually with the next clause 奈何以死惧之.
usage.zh: 多见于政论、史论；常接“奈何以死惧之”。

pinyin: bù tān wéi bǎo
literal: not · be greedy · as · treasure
natural: count non-greed as one's treasure

meaning.en: To treat freedom from greed as the real treasure; a byword for integrity in office.
meaning.zh: 把不贪婪当作最宝贵的品质，常用来称颂为官清廉。

examples.zh: 他以不贪为宝，一生清廉。
examples.en: He counted non-greed as his treasure and was honest all his life.

examples.zh: 干部要以不贪为宝，拒绝一切诱惑。
examples.en: Officials should count honesty above all and refuse every temptation.

examples.zh: 宋人献玉被拒，子罕说：我以不贪为宝。
examples.en: A man of Song offered jade and was refused: Zi Han said 'I treasure not being greedy'.

story.en: A man of Song offered a jade to the minister Zi Han; he refused: 'I treat not being greedy as my treasure, and you treat jade as yours; if you give it to me we both lose our treasure' (我以不贪为宝，尔以玉为宝).
story.zh: 《左传·襄公十五年》：宋人或得玉，献诸子罕，子罕弗受。子罕曰：“我以不贪为宝，尔以玉为宝，若以与我，皆丧宝也。”

usage.en: Formal; the story is of Zi Han of Song refusing a gift of jade.
usage.zh: 较正式；典故为宋国子罕拒收玉。

pinyin: yīng qí míng yǐ
literal: chirp · its · call · (particle)
natural: the bird chirps

meaning.en: A bird chirps; in the ode a metaphor for calling out for friends, usually completed with 求其友声.
meaning.zh: 鸟儿嘤嘤鸣叫，在《诗经》中比喻寻求友情。常接“求其友声”。

examples.zh: 嘤其鸣矣，求其友声，说的就是人对友情的渴望。
examples.en: 'The bird calls, seeking its friends' is about humans' longing for friendship.

examples.zh: 春天听到嘤其鸣矣的鸟声，让人想起远方的朋友。
examples.en: Hearing the birds' 'yīng qí míng yǐ' in spring makes one think of friends far away.

examples.zh: 同学会的请柬上写着“嘤其鸣矣”。
examples.en: The invitation to the class reunion carried the words 'the birds call'.

story.en: The ode 'Felling Trees' says: 'The birds chirp, seeking the voice of their friends' (嘤其鸣矣，求其友声).
story.zh: 《诗经·小雅·伐木》：“伐木丁丁，鸟鸣嘤嘤。出自幽谷，迁于乔木。嘤其鸣矣，求其友声。”

date.zh: 西周至春秋 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary; seen in invitations, couplets and letters about friendship.
usage.zh: 书面语，常见于请柬、对联和谈友情的信函。

pinyin: āi āi fù mǔ
literal: grieved · grieved · father · mother
natural: poor parents, so worn with grief

meaning.en: An expression of sorrow for the toil of one's parents, especially when they have died and cannot be repaid.
meaning.zh: 哀叹父母养育子女的辛劳，多用于父母去世、无法报答之时。

examples.zh: 哀哀父母，生我劬劳，每读此句他都泪流满面。
examples.en: 'Poor parents, how hard they toiled to bear me'; every time he read this line he wept.

examples.zh: 清明节回乡扫墓，想起哀哀父母，不禁黯然。
examples.en: Returning at Qingming to sweep the graves, he thought of his poor, toil-worn parents and was heartbroken.

examples.zh: 哀哀父母的恩情，永远报答不完。
examples.en: The kindness of one's toil-worn parents can never be fully repaid.

story.en: The ode 'Tall Artemisia' says: 'Alas for my parents! How hard they toiled in raising me' (哀哀父母，生我劬劳).
story.zh: 《诗经·小雅·蓼莪》：“哀哀父母，生我劬劳。”

date.zh: 西周至春秋 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Literary, used in mourning and filial contexts; usually followed by 生我劬劳.
usage.zh: 书面语，用于悼念和孝道语境；常接“生我劬劳”。

pinyin: guó ér wàng jiā
literal: for the state · and · forget · family
natural: put the country first and forget one's family

meaning.en: To be so devoted to the state that one forgets one's own family.
meaning.zh: 一心为国，顾不上自己的家庭。

examples.zh: 他国而忘家，常年在边疆工作，很少回家。
examples.en: He put the nation before his family and worked at the frontier, rarely getting home.

examples.zh: 古人讲国而忘家，公而忘私。
examples.en: The ancients spoke of forgetting one's family for the state and one's private interests for the public.

examples.zh: 科学家们国而忘家，隐姓埋名数十年。
examples.en: The scientists forgot their families for the nation and lived in anonymity for decades.

story.en: Jia Yi's memorial says a minister should 'forget himself for his lord, forget his family for the state, forget private interest for the public' (主而忘身，国而忘家，公而忘私).
story.zh: 《汉书·贾谊传》载贾谊《治安策》：“主而忘身，国而忘家，公而忘私。”

usage.en: Formal, usually in the series 国而忘家，公而忘私; praise of selflessness.
usage.zh: 较正式，常与“公而忘私”连用，称颂无私奉献。

pinyin: bù zì yóu wú nìng sǐ
literal: no · freedom · rather · die
natural: give me liberty or give me death

meaning.en: A slogan of those who value freedom above life.
meaning.zh: 把自由看得比生命更重要的口号。

equivalents: give me liberty or give me death

examples.zh: 他们高呼“不自由毋宁死”，投入了反抗的行列。
examples.en: They shouted 'liberty or death' and joined the resistance.

examples.zh: 不自由毋宁死，是许多革命者共同的信念。
examples.en: 'Liberty or death' was the shared belief of many revolutionaries.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师讲到了“不自由毋宁死”这句口号。
examples.en: In history class the teacher discussed the slogan 'bù zì yóu wú nìng sǐ'.

usage.en: Slogan; formal and stirring. 毋宁 is literary for 'rather'.
usage.zh: 口号，庄重有力；“毋宁”是书面语“宁可”。

pinyin: chéng xìng ér lái, bài xìng ér guī
literal: ride · high spirits · come, spoil · spirits · return
natural: come in high spirits and leave disappointed

meaning.en: To set out full of enthusiasm and come back disappointed.
meaning.zh: 兴致勃勃地去，却扫兴地回来。

equivalents: come full of hope, go away disappointed
go with high hopes and return crestfallen

examples.zh: 景区临时关门，我们乘兴而来，败兴而归。
examples.en: The scenic area closed unexpectedly, so we arrived in high spirits and left disappointed.

examples.zh: 演唱会取消了，乘兴而来，败兴而归的歌迷们议论纷纷。
examples.en: The concert was cancelled and the fans, who came cheerfully and went away dispirited, were grumbling.

examples.zh: 本想去尝尝那家老店，谁知乘兴而来，败兴而归。
examples.en: I wanted to try that old restaurant but came eagerly and left disappointed.

usage.en: Set phrase; often a rueful comment after a wasted trip. Echoes the Shishuo Xinyu story of Wang Huizhi.
usage.zh: 常用于白跑一趟后的感叹；与《世说新语》王徽之雪夜访戴的典故相关。

pinyin: qí yān jiǔ diǎn
literal: Qi · mist · nine · specks
natural: nine specks of mist

meaning.en: A bird's-eye view of China from on high, in which the nine regions look like nine tiny puffs of smoke; also, the vastness of the world.
meaning.zh: 从高处俯瞰，中国九州小得像九点烟尘，形容天地广阔、人世渺小。

equivalents: the nine provinces seen as specks
the whole land seen from on high

examples.zh: 登上山顶极目远望，齐烟九点，天地尽收眼底。
examples.en: From the summit one looks far into the distance, and the nine regions become specks of mist.

examples.zh: 站在九天之上看人间，齐烟九点，万事皆小。
examples.en: Looking down on the human world from the heavens, the whole land is nine puffs of smoke and all is small.

examples.zh: 诗人以“齐烟九点”写出宇宙的辽阔。
examples.en: The poet's phrase 'nine specks of mist' conveys the vastness of the cosmos.

story.en: In 'Dreaming of Heaven' Li He, looking down from the moon, sees 'the nine specks of smoke of the Middle Land and the sea like water poured from a cup' (遥望齐州九点烟，一泓海水杯中泻).
story.zh: 李贺《梦天》：“遥望齐州九点烟，一泓海水杯中泻。”

usage.en: Poetic; 齐 here is 齐州 (China, 'the Middle Land').
usage.zh: 诗意用语，“齐”指齐州，即中国。

pinyin: bái shǒu fāng huǐ dú shū chí
literal: white · head · only then · regret · study · late
natural: with white hair one regrets starting to study too late

meaning.en: Only when one is old does one regret not having studied earlier.
meaning.zh: 到老了才后悔读书读得太晚。

examples.zh: 黑发不知勤学早，白首方悔读书迟，同学们要珍惜时光。
examples.en: Don't wait until you're grey to regret studying late, children, so cherish your time.

examples.zh: 他中年才重新进修，感叹白首方悔读书迟。
examples.en: He went back to study only in middle age and sighed that regret comes with grey hair.

examples.zh: 白首方悔读书迟，这句诗被刻在图书馆的墙上。
examples.en: 'With white hair one regrets starting to study too late' is carved on the library wall.

story.en: Yan Zhenqing's 'Exhortation to Study': 'Black-haired, one does not know to study early; with white hair one regrets reading too late' (黑发不知勤学早，白首方悔读书迟).
story.zh: 颜真卿《劝学》：“三更灯火五更鸡，正是男儿读书时。黑发不知勤学早，白首方悔读书迟。”

usage.en: Often used to urge the young to study; first half 黑发不知勤学早.
usage.zh: 常用来劝勉年轻人勤学；上句为“黑发不知勤学早”。

pinyin: chē rú liú shuǐ mǎ rú lóng
literal: carriages · like · flowing · water, horses · like · dragons
natural: carriages like flowing water, horses like dragons

meaning.en: A scene of busy traffic and splendour: an endless stream of carriages and fine horses.
meaning.zh: 车辆像流水般不断，骏马像游龙般矫健，形容往来热闹、繁华景象。

equivalents: an endless stream of fine carriages

examples.zh: 节日的街头车如流水马如龙，热闹非凡。
examples.en: On festival days the streets teem with carriages and horses, extremely lively.

examples.zh: 回忆旧时繁华，他念起“车如流水马如龙”。
examples.en: Recalling the glory of bygone days, he recited 'carriages like flowing water, horses like dragons'.

examples.zh: 古画里的都城车如流水马如龙，满是烟火气。
examples.en: In the old painting the capital is all flowing carriages and dragon-like horses, full of life.

story.en: Li Yu, the captive last ruler of Southern Tang, recalls in 'Wang Jiangnan' the old pleasure park: 'carriages like flowing water, horses like dragons, flowers and moon in spring breeze'.
story.zh: 南唐后主李煜《望江南》：“多少恨，昨夜梦魂中。还似旧时游上苑，车如流水马如龙，花月正春风。”

date.zh: 五代十国 · 约10世纪70年代
date.en: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms, c. 970s

usage.en: Literary; can evoke nostalgia for past glory. See also the modern 车水马龙.
usage.zh: 书面语，可带怀旧意味；参见“车水马龙”。

pinyin: xī xiào nù mà jiē chéng wén zhāng
literal: play · laugh · anger · scold · all · become · writing
natural: laughter and rage alike turn into good writing

meaning.en: A skilled writer can turn any mood, whether joking, laughing, angry or abusive, into fine prose.
meaning.zh: 形容文笔高超，无论嬉笑还是怒骂，写出来都成妙文。

equivalents: a gifted writer's every mood turns to art

examples.zh: 鲁迅的杂文嬉笑怒骂皆成文章。
examples.en: Lu Xun's essays turn jest and rage alike into polished writing.

examples.zh: 评论家夸他嬉笑怒骂皆成文章。
examples.en: The critic praised him: his teasing and scolding all become good writing.

examples.zh: 嬉笑怒骂皆成文章，这是功力深厚的表现。
examples.en: Turning every tone into good writing is a sign of deep skill.

usage.en: Praise of fluent, versatile writers; traditionally said of Su Shi.
usage.zh: 称赞文章高手；传统上多指苏轼。

pinyin: jiāng yù qǔ zhī, bì xiān yǔ zhī
literal: about to · want · take · it, must · first · give · it
natural: to take something, first give something

meaning.en: If you want to take something from someone, first give them something; a tactic of conceding a little to gain a lot.
meaning.zh: 想要得到什么，必须先给予对方一些好处；先让后取的策略。

equivalents: give a little to get a lot
you have to give to get

examples.zh: 将欲取之，必先予之，公司先免费送出试用装。
examples.en: To take, first give: the company began by giving out free samples.

examples.zh: 谈判时将欲取之，必先予之，适当让步才能换来更大的回报。
examples.en: In negotiations, give first in order to take; reasonable concessions bring greater returns.

examples.zh: 将欲取之，必先予之，这也是商业竞争中的常见手段。
examples.en: 'To take, first give' is also a common tactic in business competition.

usage.en: Strategic maxim; the idea echoes Laozi ch. 36 (将欲夺之，必固与之). Can sound calculating.
usage.zh: 谋略箴言，思想与《老子》三十六章“将欲夺之，必固与之”相通；有时带算计的意味。

pinyin: qún ér bù dǎng
literal: sociable · yet · not · form factions
natural: sociable but not factional

meaning.en: To get along well with everyone without forming cliques.
meaning.zh: 与大家和睦相处，但不结党营私。

examples.zh: 君子群而不党，与人为善却不拉帮结派。
examples.en: A gentleman is sociable but not factional; friendly to all, but never forming cliques.

examples.zh: 他在单位群而不党，口碑很好。
examples.en: At work he is sociable without being partisan, and is well regarded.

examples.zh: 群而不党，才能保持公正。
examples.en: Only by being sociable without factions can one stay fair.

story.en: Confucius said: 'The gentleman is dignified but does not quarrel; sociable but not factional' (君子矜而不争，群而不党).
story.zh: 《论语·卫灵公》：“君子矜而不争，群而不党。”

usage.en: Formal; praise of a person of principle. Contrasts with 结党营私.
usage.zh: 较正式，称赞有原则的人；与“结党营私”相对。

pinyin: jū wú qiú ān
literal: dwelling · not · seek · comfort
natural: not seeking comfort in one's home

meaning.en: A person of high aims does not demand comfortable living.
meaning.zh: 有志向的人不追求居住的安逸。

equivalents: not bothered about a comfortable home

examples.zh: 君子食无求饱，居无求安，把精力放在学问上。
examples.en: A gentleman does not seek a full meal or a comfortable home, but devotes his energy to learning.

examples.zh: 他住在简陋的宿舍里，居无求安，一心做研究。
examples.en: He lived in plain dormitories, seeking no comfort, and devoted himself to research.

examples.zh: 年轻人居无求安，才可能闯出一片天地。
examples.en: Only young people who don't seek comfort at home can carve out a world of their own.

story.en: Confucius: 'A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill or to live in comfort, is quick in action and careful in speech' (君子食无求饱，居无求安).
story.zh: 《论语·学而》：“君子食无求饱，居无求安，敏于事而慎于言，就有道而正焉，可谓好学也已。”

usage.en: Often paired with 食无求饱; formal, in praise of frugality for study or work.
usage.zh: 常与“食无求饱”连用，较正式，称赞为学或事业而不讲究生活。

pinyin: fēi zhì wú yǐ chéng xué
literal: without · ambition · no · means · complete · learning
natural: without ambition one cannot complete one's studies

meaning.en: Without firm ambition you cannot succeed in your studies.
meaning.zh: 没有远大志向，就不能学有所成。

examples.zh: 非志无以成学，先要有明确的目标。
examples.en: Without ambition there is no scholarship; first have a clear goal.

examples.zh: 老师勉励大家“非志无以成学”。
examples.en: The teacher encouraged everyone: 'without ambition, no learning'.

examples.zh: 他读书靠的是一股志气，应了那句非志无以成学。
examples.en: He studied on sheer determination, living up to the saying 'without ambition, no learning'.

story.en: In his 'Letter to His Son' Zhuge Liang wrote: 'Without study talent cannot broaden, and without ambition study cannot succeed'.
story.zh: 诸葛亮《诫子书》：“非学无以广才，非志无以成学。”

usage.en: Usually coupled with 非学无以广才; mottoes and educational writing.
usage.zh: 常与“非学无以广才”连用，多见于校训、教育文字。

pinyin: xíng jǐ yǒu chǐ
literal: conduct · oneself · have · sense of shame
natural: act with a sense of shame

meaning.en: To behave with a sense of shame, never doing what one would be ashamed of.
meaning.zh: 做事要有羞耻之心，不做不光彩的事。

equivalents: keep a sense of shame in one's conduct

examples.zh: 读书人当行己有耻，不做违背良心的事。
examples.en: A scholar should act with a sense of shame and never go against conscience.

examples.zh: 行己有耻，是他一生遵循的准则。
examples.en: 'Conduct oneself with a sense of shame' was the rule he lived by.

examples.zh: 面对诱惑，要做到行己有耻。
examples.en: When facing temptation, keep to a sense of shame in your conduct.

story.en: Zigong asked what makes a true scholar-official; Confucius said: 'One who conducts himself with a sense of shame and does not disgrace his lord's commission abroad' (行己有耻，使于四方，不辱君命，可谓士矣).
story.zh: 《论语·子路》：“行己有耻，使于四方，不辱君命，可谓士矣。”

usage.en: Formal; moral exhortation. Gu Yanwu made it a motto of scholarship.
usage.zh: 较正式，用于道德劝勉；顾炎武曾以此为学人准则。

pinyin: rú lín shēn yuān, rú lǚ bó bīng
literal: as if · overlooking · deep · abyss, as if · treading · thin · ice
natural: as if standing at an abyss, as if treading on thin ice

meaning.en: To act with the greatest caution and anxiety, as if on the edge of danger.
meaning.zh: 形容做事极为小心谨慎，如同面临危险。

examples.zh: 接手这个项目时，他如临深渊，如履薄冰。
examples.en: When he took over the project he felt as if at the edge of an abyss, treading on thin ice.

examples.zh: 在高压监管下，企业只能如临深渊，如履薄冰地经营。
examples.en: Under tight regulation the firms can only operate as though on thin ice.

examples.zh: 她生怕出错，每天如临深渊，如履薄冰。
examples.en: Afraid of slipping up, she lives every day on tenterhooks.

story.en: The ode 'Xiao Min' ends: 'Be fearful and cautious, as if facing a deep abyss, as if treading on thin ice' (战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰).
story.zh: 《诗经·小雅·小旻》：“不敢暴虎，不敢冯河。人知其一，莫知其他。战战兢兢，如临深渊，如履薄冰。”

date.zh: 西周至春秋 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: Full couplet; the halves also exist as separate chengyu (如临深渊, 如履薄冰). Usually predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 完整对句，两半也各自成语（如临深渊、如履薄冰）；多作谓语或状语。

pinyin: rén xīn wéi wēi
literal: human · mind · is · precarious
natural: the human mind is precarious

meaning.en: The human heart is unpredictable and prone to error, so it needs guidance.
meaning.zh: 人的内心难测，容易动摇出错，需要引导约束。

examples.zh: 人心惟危，道心惟微，治国修身都要谨慎。
examples.en: The human mind is precarious and the mind of the Way subtle, so rulers and individuals both need care.

examples.zh: 人心惟危，制度必须有防范措施。
examples.en: The human mind is precarious, so the system must have safeguards.

examples.zh: 面对巨大利益，才知人心惟危。
examples.en: Only when huge interests are at stake do we see how precarious the human heart is.

story.en: In the 'Counsels of the Great Yu': 'The human mind is perilous, the mind of the Way is subtle; be refined, be single-minded, hold firmly to the middle'.
story.zh: 《尚书·大禹谟》：“人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允执厥中。”

date.zh: 东晋 · 4世纪（晚出古文《尚书》）

usage.en: Literary; usually quoted with 道心惟微. Often invoked in discussions of institutions and ethics.
usage.zh: 书面语，常与“道心惟微”连用；多用于谈制度与伦理。

pinyin: shì ér bù jiàn, tīng ér bù wén
literal: look · yet · not · see, listen · yet · not · hear
natural: look without seeing, listen without hearing

meaning.en: To fail to notice what is in front of one's eyes and ears because one's mind is elsewhere or one chooses to ignore it.
meaning.zh: 心思不在，或故意不理，对眼前耳边的事物毫不在意。

equivalents: look without seeing and listen without hearing
turn a blind eye and a deaf ear

examples.zh: 他心里有事，对周围的一切视而不见，听而不闻。
examples.en: His mind on other things, he saw and heard nothing around him.

examples.zh: 对群众的意见视而不见，听而不闻，是不负责任的表现。
examples.en: To look past and listen past the public's views is irresponsible.

examples.zh: 她沉浸在书里，视而不见，听而不闻。
examples.en: Lost in her book, she was blind and deaf to the world.

story.en: The Great Learning: 'When the mind is not present, one looks and does not see, listens and does not hear, eats and does not know the taste' (心不在焉，视而不见，听而不闻，食而不知其味).
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“所谓修身在正其心者……心不在焉，视而不见，听而不闻，食而不知其味。”

usage.en: Full couplet; the halves also exist as 视而不见 and 听而不闻. Predicate or complement.
usage.zh: 完整对句，两半也各自成语；多作谓语或补语。

pinyin: wú suǒ cuò shǒu zú
literal: no · place · to put · hands · feet
natural: not knowing where to put one's hands and feet

meaning.en: To be at a complete loss as to what to do, with nothing one can safely do.
meaning.zh: 不知道该怎么办才好，无所适从。

examples.zh: 突如其来的变化让大家无所措手足。
examples.en: The sudden change left everyone at a loss.

examples.zh: 政策朝令夕改，使百姓无所措手足。
examples.en: Policies changed daily and the people did not know where to turn.

examples.zh: 他第一次上台，紧张得无所措手足。
examples.en: On stage for the first time he was so nervous that he didn't know what to do with himself.

story.en: Confucius: 'When punishments are not just, the people do not know where to put hand or foot' (刑罚不中，则民无所措手足).
story.zh: 《论语·子路》：“名不正则言不顺……刑罚不中，则民无所措手足。”

usage.en: Literary, often with 使/令 + 人 + 无所措手足; the everyday forms are 手足无措 and 不知所措.
usage.zh: 书面语，常说“使人无所措手足”；日常多说“手足无措”“不知所措”。

pinyin: yuè yùn ér fēng, chǔ rùn ér yǔ
literal: moon · halo · then · wind, plinth · damp · then · rain
natural: a halo round the moon means wind, damp plinths mean rain

meaning.en: Small signs foretell what is coming: a ring round the moon means wind, and damp stone bases mean rain.
meaning.zh: 见到细微的征兆，就能预知将要发生的事。

examples.zh: 月晕而风，础润而雨，有经验的人能从蛛丝马迹中看出趋势。
examples.en: A halo means wind and damp plinths mean rain: experienced people read trends from slight clues.

examples.zh: 农民说月晕而风，础润而雨，看天气全凭经验。
examples.en: Farmers say a ring round the moon brings wind and damp plinths bring rain; they judge the weather by experience.

examples.zh: 分析师常说月晕而风，础润而雨，市场早有征兆。
examples.en: Analysts often say there are always omens: ring round the moon, rain on the way.

story.en: Su Xun's 'Discerning Treachery' (traditional attribution) says: 'A halo round the moon brings wind, damp plinths bring rain, and everyone knows this' (月晕而风，础润而雨，人人知之).
story.zh: 苏洵《辨奸论》（传为苏洵作）：“月晕而风，础润而雨，人人知之。”

usage.en: Literary proverb of weather lore, extended to omens. Follows the line 人人知之.
usage.zh: 书面谚语，由天气经验引申为见微知著；下文接“人人知之”。
